- **Fromm, Ludaic & Elofsson, "Evaluating deep learning based structure prediction methods on antibody–antigen complexes."** *Bioinformatics* 42(4):btag136, online 21 Mar 2026. DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag136. On 110 unseen Ab–Ag complexes: AF3 > AF2.3, Boltz-1, Chai-1. Two findings matter operationally: (i) increased sampling improves the chance of generating a correct model **roughly log-linearly**, but (ii) AlphaFold's internal confidence often cannot identify its own best model, so top-1 performance lags best-of-N substantially. AF3 degrades sharply on complexes lacking structural similarity to training data. Code: `github.com/samuelfromm/abag-benchmark-set`; data Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.17978681.

- **Hitawala & Gray, "What does AlphaFold3 learn about antibody and nanobody docking, and what remains unsolved?"** *mAbs* 17(1):2545601, 14 Aug 2025. DOI 10.1080/19420862.2025.2545601. AF3 median CDR-H3 RMSD **2.52 Å** (vs IgFold 3.0 Å, AF2.3-M 2.83 Å, Boltz-1 3.78 Å, Chai-1 3.63 Å). High-quality docking success rises from 2.4% (AF2.3-M) to 10.2% (AF3) — i.e. a ~65% outright failure rate at single-seed sampling.

- **"A Structural Antibody Benchmark of AlphaFold3 reveals Hallucinated Epitopes and a Bias for Orderness."** bioRxiv, posted ~30 Jul 2026, DOI 10.64898/2026.07.30.741792 (also surfaced in PubMed). The largest-scale screen I found: 3,401 SAbDab complexes + 23,798 negative controls. Max recall **53%** at 100 inference seeds; innate false-positive rate ~**3%**, with AF3 hallucinating plausible interfaces across decoy surfaces while avoiding disordered regions. Accuracy falls with antigen size/surface area; X-ray-derived antibodies predicted better than EM-derived. Importantly, **~34% of false negatives still had the correct epitope** despite poor structural alignment.

- **Peng et al., "A comprehensive benchmarking of AlphaFold3 for predicting biomacromolecules and their interactions."** *Brief. Bioinform.* 26(6):bbaf616, 28 Nov 2025. DOI 10.1093/bib/bbaf616. AF3 clearly beats AF-Multimer on antigen–antibody interfaces.

- **"Benchmarking antibody modeling tools across structure prediction, docking, and paratope–epitope interface analysis."** *Bioinformatics Advances* (PubMed). ImmuneBuilder, IgFold, AF3, GRAMM, dyMEAN on 50 humanized complexes: AF3 best overall and for CDR-H3; medium/high-quality interfaces for only **46%** of complexes. When docking succeeded, AF3 recovered epitope/paratope residues and salt bridges well but hydrogen bonds and fine contact strengths poorly. Data: Zenodo record 20710876.

- **"Benchmarking AlphaFold and related deep learning approaches for modeling antibody and TCR antigen recognition."** bioRxiv. Antibody–**peptide** complexes remain the hardest class despite small antigen size; model pooling across methods raised near-native success from **41% → 59%**.

## 2. The real bottleneck is ranking, not sampling — hence a wave of rescoring papers

This is the clearest trend in the 2025–2026 literature: several groups independently concluded AF3 generates near-native models it then discards.

- **ABAG-Rank** (*Bioinformatics*) — DeepSets-based, permutation-invariant ranking over variable-sized AF decoy ensembles; simple geometric descriptors + AF confidence beat AF3 internal scoring. Code: `github.com/tadteo/ABAG-Rank`, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.21132090.
- **DeepRank-Ab** (*Communications Biology*) — geometric deep learning scoring trained on ~2.3M decoys from 1,442 complexes; **+35.5% AF3 top-1 success**, >2× mean top-1 DockQ, 100% top-5 on external CAPRI Ab–Ag targets.
- **TINA** (*Acta Pharmacologica Sinica*) — many-body (2/3/4-body) atom-level interface tensors for post-hoc ranking of AF3 pools; benefit largest in low-confidence and antibody-related cases where ipTM is uninformative.
- **ProTact** (*Communications Biology*) — SE(3)-invariant GNN with physics-informed geometric complementarity; +30.5% over AF3 default confidence in low-MSA contexts.
- **AFilter** (bioRxiv, 16 Aug 2026, DOI 10.64898/2026.08.16.745116) — ML-optimized interface-energy filtering of AF3 epitope predictions; removes >90% of false predictions while keeping >90% of true positives.

## 3. Sampling- and input-side interventions (no retraining)

- **"Sequence Scanning Improves Accuracy for Antibody-Antigen and Molecular Glue Ternary Complex Cofolding"** (*ChemMedChem*) — systematic constraints to diversify sampling, evaluated on Boltz and Protenix.
- **"Computational Modeling of Antibody-Antigen Complexes: PLM-Based and MSA-Based Approaches"** (arXiv thesis) — two AF3-compatible interventions: CDR-focused MSA refinement with depth recovery, and convergence-aware recycling. Consistent gains over the AF3 baseline **without weight access or retraining**. Also a useful negative result: single-sequence PLM embeddings do *not* transfer from monomer to complex prediction — no antibody/antigen co-evolutionary signal means no reliable interface identification.

## 4. Unbound Fv / antibody-only prediction

- **ImmuneBuilder** (ABodyBuilder2/NanoBodyBuilder2/TCRBuilder2), *Communications Biology* — still the speed/accuracy reference point: CDR-H3 at 2.81 Å, >100× faster than AF-Multimer. **ABodyBuilder3** (arXiv 2405.20863) adds language-model embeddings and a predicted-LDDT output.
- **FlashABB**, "Modelling antibody structures at the speed of language," bioRxiv 3 Jun 2026, DOI 10.64898/2026.06.03.729879 — ABodyBuilder2/3-comparable backbones at much higher throughput.
- **BALM/BALMFold** and **xTrimoABFold** (arXiv) — antibody-language-model folding, reported to beat AF2/IgFold/ESMFold/OmegaFold on antibody benchmarks.
- **Igloo** (arXiv) — multimodal CDR-loop tokenizer; +5.9% on H3 loop retrieval, extends canonical-cluster coverage, and improves PLM affinity prediction on 8/10 targets.
- Review: **Greenshields-Watson et al., "Challenges and compromises: Predicting unbound antibody structures with deep learning,"** *Curr. Opin. Struct. Biol.* 90:102983 (2025). DOI 10.1016/j.sbi.2025.102983.

## 5. Nanobodies as a distinct, harder problem

- **"Combining AI Structure Prediction and Integrative Modeling for Nanobody-Antigen Complexes"** (*JCIM*) — HADDOCK ensemble docking from AF2 + ImmuneBuilder models beats the AF baseline on all generated models, **provided some epitope information is available**.
- **"Analysing open-source protein folding models for nanobody binding prediction"** (*Frontiers in Bioinformatics*) — Boltz-2, Chai-1, IntFold, AF3 on binder-vs-bait ranking across 17 antigens plus CDR alanine-scan OOD detection. **Boltz-2 confidence measures ranked true binders best**; local metrics (pLDDT, CDR/interface-focused) were best for OOD detection. No single metric won both tasks, and all models generalized poorly to unseen antigens.
- **Eshak et al., "Advancements in Nanobody Epitope Prediction: AlphaFold2Multimer vs AlphaFold3,"** *JCIM* 65(4):1782–1797, 10 Feb 2025.
- bioRxiv 2025–2026: "Improving nanobody structure prediction with self-distillation" (2 Dec 2025, 10.64898/2025.12.01.691162); "Disulphide and sequence-encoded conformational priors guide nanobody structure prediction" (13 Feb 2026, 10.64898/2026.02.13.705647 — compares AF3, Boltz-1, NBB2, NbForge on 47 held-out nanobodies); "Assessing Structural Prediction Accuracy for Nanobody–Small Molecule Complexes" (12 Dec 2025).

## 6. Training-data scarcity and co-folding ensembles

- **SprintX** (*mAbs*) — a large AF3-generated synthetic Ab–Ag complex dataset with multi-stage QC (confidence, stereochemistry, interface contacts), released openly as structural prior knowledge for pretraining. Positioned as a complement to, not a replacement for, experimental structures.
- **"Benchmarking antibody-antigen co-folding on human monomeric antigens"** — bioRxiv 24 Aug 2026, DOI 10.64898/2026.08.20.745880; ten co-folding protocols.
- **SoupFold**, "Co-folding with a Soup of Representations" — arXiv 2609.15552 (Sep 2026), ensembling representations across co-folding models.
- **DeepAAAssembly**, "High-accuracy structural modeling of antibody-antigen complexes" — *Communications Biology* (2026), DOI 10.1038/s42003-026-10757-0; +10.7% mean DockQ over AF3 on 67 complexes.

## 7. Adjacent / applied

- **AF3 for TCR-mimic Fv–pMHC** (*mAbs* 18(1), Dec 2026, DOI 10.1080/19420862.2026.2719263): ~**50%** correct prediction rate, explicitly described as on par with AF3 on Ab–Ag and Nb–Ag.
- **Developability**: "Predicting antibody self-association with sequence-structure fusion models" (*mAbs*) — ESM-2 + AF-structure residue graphs; VHH F1 = 0.76, IgG F1 = 0.57 on edit-distance-controlled splits of 1,499 IgGs / 841 VHHs.
- **OpenAntigens** (*Nucleic Acids Research*) — construct-design database for 5,328 human secreted/membrane proteins using AlphaFold pLDDT and PAE to set domain boundaries; openantigens.org.

## ANSWER

Recent AlphaFold/antibody-structure literature (2025–Nov 2026) converges on five points:

1. **AF3 is the current best general-purpose option** for antibody and nanobody structure and docking — median CDR-H3 ~2.5 Å, beating IgFold, AF2.3-M, Boltz-1 and Chai-1 (Hitawala & Gray, *mAbs* 2025, DOI 10.1080/19420862.2025.2545601; Fromm et al., *Bioinformatics* 42(4):btag136, DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag136).
2. **Complex-level accuracy is still poor**: ~65% single-seed docking failure, max recall 53% even at 100 seeds, ~3% hallucinated-interface false-positive rate, medium/high-quality interfaces for only ~46% of complexes (bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.30.741792; *Bioinformatics Advances* benchmark).
3. **Model selection, not sampling, is the bottleneck** — sampling gains are log-linear but AF's own confidence can't pick its best model. Hence a 2025–2026 wave of external rescorers: DeepRank-Ab (+35.5% AF3 top-1), ABAG-Rank, TINA, ProTact (+30.5% in low-MSA), AFilter.
4. **Fast antibody-only predictors remain competitive and far cheaper**: ImmuneBuilder/ABodyBuilder3, FlashABB, BALMFold, xTrimoABFold, Igloo.
5. **Nanobodies are a separate, harder problem**, with dedicated 2026 work (self-distillation, disulphide/conformational priors, NbForge) and evidence that **Boltz-2 confidence beats AF3 for nanobody binder ranking** (*Front. Bioinform.*).

Dates/DOIs above are from a web-search agent, not a structured database; flag the PAbFold and SoupFold entries as unverified.
